headline: The untouched renderer, photographed for the first time.
note: Not a build round. This is the harness proving it can boot the real page, place a 172-tile district through the shipped tryPlace() path and photograph it — the thing that lets every later round be judged on output instead of on a diff. What it shows: five residential archetypes on a seeded street grid, procedural canvas textures, a lamp-lit road network — and a global violet cast that no reference frame has. The scores in the matrix for this row are the lead's own read of the baseline frames, recorded so later rounds have something to move against; every round from 1 on is scored by critics who did not write the code.

headline: Five builders, one file. The violet cast is gone — but there is still no sun.

note: Every piece came back BEHIND. The wins are real and local: building silhouette 7 and roads 6, both up from 4. The losses are structural — the whole-frame critic measured a sunlit wall at 21% luminance against a shaded one at 24%, a ratio of 1.14x where the reference frames run 2-3x, and called it: there is no sun in this scene. Two of the low scores were the harness's fault, not the builders'. Vehicles scored 1 and citizens 2 because manageAgents() is only ever called from animate(), rAF never fires in headless capture, and the city was photographed empty — the ten vehicle bodies and the rigged civilian existed the whole time. Fixed: the standard district now carries 29 agents, and the street camera sits on a carriageway at eye height instead of above the rooftops.

headline: The lighting round. Shadows were never being drawn at all.

pieces.title: Palette, lighting and colour grade
pieces.summary: Two independent causes, both real. Shadows were never drawn: three r171's WebGPU node pipeline computes a shadow from the shadow target's COLOUR attachment, the WebGL2 backend runs that pass depth-only, so the term collapsed to a constant 1.0 - the depth pass was drawn every frame and thrown away. And the sun spent every afternoon behind the camera: of 2,232 wall samples at 15:00, fourteen were sunlit.
pieces.gap: Get traffic and pedestrians into the captured PIXELS, not just the simulation. Round 2 carried 29 agents and produced zero visible vehicles and zero visible citizens across three frames.

note: 🔴 THESE SCORES ARE AGAINST THE WRONG FRAME, and the fault is the harness's. estClock() reads the real wall clock - "the sun rises when YOUR sun rises" - so every round was photographed at whatever time of day the capture happened to run. r0 and r1 landed mid-afternoon; r2 landed at 20:17. The lighting work was MEASURED at 15:00 and PHOTOGRAPHED at night, and manageAgents() culls the crowd at nightfall - which is why a round that moved the sunlit:shaded ratio from 1.11x to 2.67x and terrain luminance from 0.215 to 0.527 scored 4/10 for lighting and 0/10 for vehicles. The hour is now pinned as a harness constant and the frames above have been re-captured at 15:00; the scores are left as the critics gave them, because re-scoring my own work against a better frame is not a critic's verdict. Round 3 re-judges.

headline: Four camera bugs, not one art bug. The crowd finally reaches the film.

pieces.title: The crowd
pieces.summary: Four independent bugs, none in the art. The crowd was spawned into a city that did not exist yet (finishAll() calls manageAgents(), so the census was satisfied when the road network was two tiles long — all 29 agents on 3 unique positions in one corner). Nothing ever stepped them: agentTick runs only from animate(), and 2 rAF callbacks fired in 2 wall seconds. Every one of them was invisible: cullAgents() had last run against the BOOT camera and the stale visible=false rode into all three shots. And the street frame could not have contained them anyway — OrbitControls clamps maxPolarAngle to 82.8 degrees, so any eye-level request came out at y 2.3, above every roof.
pieces.gap: No vehicle is ever on a carriageway. In the street frame all four cars are parked on the FOOTWAY — past the kerb and past the grass verge, wheels on the same grey sidewalk slab the pedestrian walks on (s_place.png makes the section unambiguous: asphalt, white edge line, lavender kerb, green verge, s

pieces.title: The two artefacts
pieces.summary: Neither was the bug its symptom named. The street text was never mirrored — rotating the r2 aerial 180 degrees makes it read perfectly. The reading direction was a CONSTANT while the aerial camera sees east-west and north-south as opposite screen directions, so half the city read backwards. And the plum sky was no hex: no hue in the SKY table is magenta, the mauve was manufactured by lerping a warm-red dusk into a violet-black night. The hard seam is not a material boundary at all — the plate and the plain are the same hex in the same material; it is the fog ramp compressed by a grazing view angle.

pieces.title: The Outside chip
pieces.summary: The one defect nobody had fixed, because the agent assigned to it died mid-response. It sat exactly on the railbar pill row, invisible and unclickable. Now proven with elementsFromPoint returning the chip and a real unscripted click — and it is legible in the round-3 street frame: CITY IS CUT OFF, build a Highway Interchange on the north edge.

note: Mean 3.64 to 4.57, the largest jump of the loop, and vehicles went 0 to 4-6 and citizens 0 to 3-5. The pattern of this round is worth naming: every single defect was diagnosed to a DIFFERENT cause than its symptom suggested. A pixel diff of the rendered buffer — with-crowd against without-crowd, exactly 0 of 1,440,000 pixels different — found in one run what two rounds of art work could not. Stranger test is still 'instantly', and the next priority is the one dimension that has never moved: the plot, at 2/10. Buildings sit on a continuous flat pad with no parcel, and the whole-frame critic says that single fact is why the city reads as models on a board.

headline: Parcels landed. A critic still could not see a single property line.

pieces.title: Parcels and the setback
pieces.summary: Rounds 2-3 had already built the whole plot kit — apron, path, drive, lawn, hedge, bins, garden tree — and almost none of it was visible: a detached villa's eaves stood at z .275 against a boundary at .465, and the road aprons .110 of footway over the front, leaving ~.115 of garden a camera could see in front of a house up to 1.36 tall. The mass now slides back inside its own tile before the plot is drawn. Visible front garden goes .115 to .197, +71%. A new /src/parcel layer gives every NON-housing building a surface, a drive to the kerb on the side its door is on, a lot line and a class-appropriate boundary. Cost: +1.7% triangles, two new draw calls for the entire city.
pieces.gap: There is no parcel between the building and the kerb: the sidewalk slab abuts the front steps directly, so there is no lawn, no path from the door, and no driveway anywhere in the city — and no lot line separates neighbours. Build it as: a 4–6 m front setback per residential building; fill it with a

pieces.title: The failing economy round
pieces.summary: Decided on evidence, not taste: transit is a LICENCE like bank and founds no business. BUILDINGS.busstop/trainstation/railtrack each carry transitLicence and transitOwns() gates placement on holding the row, so the operation IS the permission and the network is the product; and revenue is already modelled by routes.js ledger(), clamped to net = min(0, fares - upkeep). A firm on op_bus would be a second, unclamped income for carrying the same passengers - the exact double-count that disqualified forge, indexfund and holdco. The clamp and a business cannot both be true. The suite is green.

note: Mean 4.57 to 4.83 and the economy suite went green, but the whole-frame critic called the project PLATEAUING and showed its working: gain per round has fallen from +1.0 to +0.2, and the score column splits cleanly in two. Everything about OBJECTS has climbed and is nearly done - silhouette 4-7-6-6-6, roads 4-6-6-7-7, street furniture 3-5-6-6-7. Everything about the WORLD BETWEEN objects has never left the floor - the plot 3-4-2-2-3, citizens 2-2-0-3-2, zoning read 2-2-3-3-3, UI 4-2-2-2-2. Its stranger-test sentence is the whole diagnosis: THE GROUND IS ONE FLAT COLOUR AND NOTHING IS ROOTED IN IT - over half the frame at every camera, and the only surface that is wrong at all three zoom levels. Round 4 built setbacks, lawns, drives, hedges and lot lines, and the plot critic still answered 'no, I cannot see where one property ends and the next begins, anywhere, in any frame'. Parcels drawn on a single uniform plane do not read as parcels. The plane is the problem, and round 5 attacks only that.

headline: The ground stopped being one flat colour. The loop stopped here.

pieces.title: The ground
pieces.summary: The map plate stopped being 576 flat constant-coloured quads and became one shared vertex lattice carrying two colour ramps blended by an independent moisture field, with real relief and a generated seamless grain map. Measured on the real captures: aerial patch-to-patch value spread +85%, hue spread +195%, near-to-far spread +429%, local contrast +117%. The MEAN was deliberately held at round 4's value — only the spread moved. No new draw calls: the rebuild is inside the plate's existing single mesh.
pieces.gap: Boundaries. The critic still could not find one place where property A's ground stops and property B's starts, at the cameras the game renders at.

pieces.title: The verdict
pieces.summary: STOP AND CHANGE APPROACH. The critic's evidence: rubric sums r3=53, r4=55, r5=56 on its own consistent scale — five rounds of hand-authored geometry bought +0.08 on the last iteration. And two consecutive rounds shipped commits titled 'give every building a parcel' and 'give every lot an edge' while it could not see a lot edge in either at the game's own camera. Its words: the loop is now producing work that satisfies the commit message and not the image.

note: 🔴 THE LOOP STOPS HERE, on the critic's recommendation and its evidence, not on a budget. The named sentence from round 4 — 'the ground is one flat colour and nothing is rooted in it' — is DEAD, and the pixels settle it: a single sightline down the aerial ground plane read 133/146/124 luminance in r4, a 22-unit random wobble with no depth direction; in r5 the same three pixels read 143/131/93, a monotonic 50-unit falloff. Across 30k grass samples the far/mid/near spread went 2.7 to 28.9, and distinct colours 261 to 3472. The fix worked and the stranger test did not move, which is the ceiling of the technique showing from the other side. The critic's three recommendations, in its order: (1) change the shot protocol — every claimed feature must be legible in a 1:1 crop at the default camera, and diff the framings, because this round's ground work never reached the street frame at all and nobody noticed; (2) take the free five points in UI legibility, which has scored 2 for four straight rounds while every round went after 3D, is the first thing a stranger sees, and is pure 2D layout with zero engine risk; (3) the real answer — an asset pipeline, glTF kits GPU-instanced in place of code-assembled primitives, the only change that moves silhouette, surface, vehicles, vegetation, furniture and zoning read together and the only one that can reach 8. Recommendation (1) is DONE — .gauntlet/capture.mjs now diffs every framing against the previous round and warns when one barely moved; run against r4 it independently reproduced the finding: aerial 48.9% changed, district 35%, street 4%.

headline: The free five points were real. Fixing the UI removed the excuse, not the gap.

pieces.title: UI legibility — 2 to 6
pieces.summary: Fourteen identical counters became one 44px strip: city, clock, four figures each with a per-hour RATE, seven service dots. Which four was read off the game's own model rather than taste - vitalsTick grows population only at >=90% coverage of food, water and health and sheds below 60%, so those are the stores on the bar and health is a dot. The old topbar was RE-HOMED as a popover rather than rebuilt, so updateHUD's writes and the vault delegation keep working untouched. 32 of 32 controls verified returning themselves from elementsFromPoint at two viewport sizes.
pieces.gap: The clock was moved off the status bar into the popover, and there is still no pause/speed control - reference frame 4 has both. The 1:59:47 left visible in the rail is a battle countdown a stranger will read as the city clock.

pieces.title: The demand panel
pieces.summary: The critic's words: the strongest single thing built in six rounds, and on causal honesty it EXCEEDS the CS2 reference. Four arrow meters with signed causal lists, and every expanded cause prints the call it was read from - 'read from /src/economy snapshot().satisfaction'. Nothing fabricated. Taxes, Gas Station Availability and Land Value are argued ABSENT in writing, because node-city has no tax rate, no fuel retail and nothing computing land value, so a plausible bar would have been a lie.

pieces.title: Round 5's regressions
pieces.summary: The tree pit was never deleted - makeTree2's paved branch is byte-for-byte round 4's, and the tile lost a Math.random coin flip between two captures. Tree tiles are now seeded on the tile like makeHousing, and the ground treatment is decided by ADJACENCY: a road on any side gets the kerbed pit, open ground gets a feathered patch. Street furniture back to 7.

note: Mean 4.67 to 5.08 and UI 2 to 6, so the round-5 critic's prediction was half-right - it called 2 to 7. The finding is what did NOT change. Stranger test is still 'instantly' for the sixth round, but WHAT lands first has moved: in round 5 the eye hit a wall of sixteen identical 410065408s and read 'someone's debug build' before it read 'city'; now the chrome is dismissed in one saccade and the first thing that registers is the junction and the row houses. In the critic's words, the read was never chrome-limited - fixing the UI did not change the answer, it only removed the excuse. Its verdict: dimension 12 was the last thing on the board fixable by writing code around the existing kit. One cheap round remains (the plot, at 3), and after that every dimension still under the bar is blocked on modelled geometry rather than on cleverness - 'you do not get from a 3-pixel stick to a citizen with a backpack and a cast shadow by writing more procedural code against primitives'. It puts the pipeline's realistic ceiling at a mean around 5.5 and a hard cap near 6 on any dimension whose 10 is modelled detail.

headline: The boundaries were built and 2.5x too short. And the ceiling estimate was wrong.

pieces.title: The plot, measured instead of rebuilt
pieces.summary: Rounds 4 and 5 built the boundary correctly and nobody measured it. A citizen here is .26 tall and a storey .34; the hedge topped out at .086 - 0.58m at that scale, ankle height - which is why three critics could not see a property line that was genuinely there. Heights roughly doubled and every run now ENDS at a capped masonry corner post. Measuring it turned up three real bugs: bt/edge/sEdge were declared hundreds of lines BELOW the drive that has to fit inside them, so privet grew up through the driveway of every hedged plot in the city; the cottage's flank palings stood on `edge` while their rail was laid on `sEdge`, so every side fence merged with the neighbour's mirror image into one unbroken run down the block - literally the 'identical ribbon running past the gap' the round-4 critic reported, still in the code three rounds later; and the 'dropped kerb' claimed since round 4 was laid UNDER the driveway, 7 thou below the thing covering it, so it had never once been visible.
pieces.gap: Still invisible at 1:1, and for a LIGHTING reason rather than a modelling one: the side yard sits permanently in its own house's shadow at luminance 20-50, so a dark hedge inside a near-black band has no contrast left to spend.

pieces.title: The four on-screen corrections
pieces.summary: The unweighted term that pinned Commercial at 100% and cascaded into Industrial, the two water models giving opposite verdicts 400px apart on one screen, the clock that had left the status bar, and a plus sign on a label every player reads as negative. All four fixed in the 2D layer, none costing a triangle.

note: 🔴 THE CLOSING CRITIC OVERTURNED THE STOP RECOMMENDATION, and showed its working. Round 6's critic had said the pipeline was capped near a mean of 5.5 with 'a hard cap around 6 on any dimension whose 10 is modelled detail', and that the next decision was to fund an asset kit. Round 7 scored 5.17 against a predicted 5.3, so on the surface that looked vindicated. The closing critic called it a trap: dimension 3, building silhouette, IS nothing but modelled detail and is at 7 today, procedurally, with no asset kit - the pipeline has already cleared the cap it was said to be under. Its own diagnosis of what is actually holding the mean down: citizens at 2 is a REGRESSION, not a limit (six readable pedestrians in round 6, zero in round 7) and recovering it is a bug fix worth +0.25 mean for zero triangles; density read is blocked on content variety, not geometry; and the plot is blocked on LOT PITCH plus a material choice, not on boundary props - widen the pitch and draw the side boundary in the light kerb concrete the driveway already uses instead of dark hedge. Its number: the realistic ceiling is a mean of 6.3-6.6, not 5.5, and the path from 5.17 to about 6.0 costs NO NEW ART. Its decision, quoted: do not fund the asset kit this round; there is roughly a full point of mean sitting in layout and content variety, which is cheaper than art and which the team has demonstrably been good at. The real wall is narrow and specific - window reveals and sills, car glazing and rims, tree crowns needing cards - and those three will pin the mean near 6.5 and keep 8+ permanently out of reach.

headline: The crowd 'regression' was a coin flip. The ceiling estimate held.

pieces.title: The crowd — diagnosed before it was built
pieces.summary: There was no regression. A with-crowd/without-crowd pixel diff read 2,934px, and forcing every agent visible read 2,934px — identical, so nothing was hidden by culling, by 'inside', or by round 7's taller boundaries. The decisive test: git archive of the r6-era tree into a scratch root, same diagnostic — statistically identical to HEAD, 29 agents, exactly 14 civilians, same scatter. Fourteen pedestrians over 100 road tiles is one per seven, and whether a 220x100 crop contains one is a coin flip that r6 won and r7 lost. Two critics scored variance. The fix is a STANDING crowd — the argument /src/parking already won for vehicles: 78 tile-seeded figures on footway and kerb, placed against MythicParking.spots() so nobody stands inside a parked car. Cost +24 meshes for 78 people, because a standing figure needs no rig and bakes into merged buckets; as agents the same 78 would have been +1,326.
pieces.gap: They are all the same figure, in one frozen stance, at 1.5-2x oversize — a pedestrian reaches 60% of a lamp mast and stands taller than the sidewalk is wide.

pieces.title: The speech bubbles
pieces.summary: Four faults, all found by driving it. The spawn test ran ONCE and then for 5.2s the speaker was free to walk indoors, be culled or leave frame while the bubble kept captioning empty pavement. 'In frame' also is not 'visible' — a line still sat on a five-storey facade with its speaker behind it, so a rate-limited raycast now answers whether the player can actually see them. The filter that makes that work is isMesh: Raycaster hits Lines, and this scene has a GridHelper lying flat over the whole map, so with it in, 0 of 9 street candidates survived and the feature went silent citywide. Found by running it, not by reading it.

pieces.title: Massing, and the paint comes off the road
pieces.summary: Three zone-legible recipes — retail fascia with a glazing strip, a flat industrial shed with a dock apron and yard, a surface car park with bay lines — and the street names finally lifted off the carriageway. Density read 4 to 6.

note: Mean 5.17 to 5.67, the biggest jump since round 3, and the 6.3-6.6 ceiling estimate is NOT falsified. The critic's test for telling 'the estimate was wrong' from 'the work did not land' is the best piece of reasoning in the loop: if the ceiling were wrong, the targeted dimensions would have REFUSED TO MOVE — you would fix the crowd and citizens would crawl 3 to 4 because the mesh itself caps it. Instead all four moved, fast and cheap: citizens 2 to 5.5, density read 4 to 6, the plot 4 to 5, surface detail 5 to 6. Its verdict: do not fund an asset kit yet, six of twelve dimensions still have a named fix costing no new geometry, and the largest is pure DOM. ⚠ UI legibility REGRESSED 6 to 4 — the demand strip lost its labels and causal lists in the massing round's layout changes, and it is now called the cheapest point on the board for the second time. Two other regressions: front-garden greenery fell from 13.9% to 8.3% of the residential band, and the standing crowd is unweighted, so people stand alone on verges beside roads running through empty fields.
